fields.title: 1. T6 — Expected Date vs. Actual Date
fields.md:
- **What was expected**: In the first round and the previous round, the expected-date field of T6 listed the oral argument date (2026-11-03) alongside 'ruling date undetermined' (Source: state.triggers_next_12m T6, Section 5 of the previous round).
- **Actual**: On 2026-11-03 (Tue), oral argument was held at the Oregon Supreme Court in Salem. Theodore J. Boutrous Jr. appeared for PacifiCorp and Nicholas Rosinia for the victims (Source: [OPB](https://www.opb.org/article/2026/11/04/wildfire-survivors-lawsuit-utility-company-fire-oregon/) 2026-11-05). The 10-Q (posted on EDGAR 2026-11-09) also states "oral argument was held on November 3, 2026" (Source: [10-Q R31](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1067983/000119312526452412/R31.htm)).
- **Two errors (honest record)**: ① The previous round rendered the 10-Q as 'stated as oral argument scheduled' — the original said 'was held' (a misreading, Source: [10-Q R31](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1067983/000119312526452412/R31.htm)). ② The ruling trigger's expected-date field listed the date of **an intermediate event that would pass**, so the measurement layer woke the engine on the argument date rather than a ruling. This round's event is itself a product of that design mistake.
- **Fix to the expectation method**: The expected-date field of a ruling trigger will contain **only one ruling checkpoint date**. New checkpoint = 2027-05-03 (estimate: oral argument + 6 months. The only basis is the report's 'within months', so the date was not set from court processing-time statistics — it is a checkpoint, not a prediction). The argument date has been moved to the trigger name and verification method fields.
